title: NavThinker: Action-Conditioned World Models for Coupled Prediction and Planning in Social Navigation
finding: HM3D SR59.46; MP3D zero-shot47.33 vs Falcon51.67. Multi-robot SR30.04,T-SR16.30 without communication.
boundary: Not an oracle gap. H-Coll and SR are different metrics. Multi-robot task differs from single-robot.

title: From Cognition to Precognition: A Future-Aware Framework for Social Navigation
section: Abstract and evaluation; local official-checkpoint scalar records separately audited
boundary: Local174 subset is not the paper evaluation or a new multi-seed reproduction.

title: PEDS: Closed-Loop Benchmarking of Social Navigation across Pedestrian Behavior Models
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters; accepted October2026 per PDF
finding: Dense-nav DRL-VO SR0.25 under HSFM vs0.55 under SocialGAIL. Dense CADRL ranges0.55-0.70. Failure taxonomy exposes collisions, freeze and timeout.
boundary: Driver changes alter environment difficulty, so spread is not guaranteed recoverable gain. Paper notes scenario-level uncertainty in rankings. Project page says20 scenarios while TableIV caption mentions21; do not rely on scenario count.

title: SHINE: Social Homology Identification for Navigation in Crowded Environments
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
finding: Topology-distinct guidance paths, learned high-level behavior selection and local contouring controller; explicit consistency mechanisms already exist.
boundary: Simple left/right/wait macro-action selection is not a new contribution by itself.

title: Proactive Local-Minima-Free Robot Navigation: Blending Motion Prediction with Safe Control
finding: MMP-MCBF safety and success10/10 in each of4 scenarios; prediction horizon can cause freezing/infeasibility. Full obstacle geometry within detection range is assumed.
boundary: Those small fully observed cases are already saturated; partially observed scenes are a different test. Strong contemporary comparator needed.

title: OA-NBV: Occlusion-Aware Next-Best-View Planning for Human-Centered Active Perception on Mobile Robots
finding: Over90% target-view acquisition success; targets single-step observation quality; multi-person extension remains future work.
boundary: View acquisition success is not social-navigation success. Optimize decision value, not target visibility alone.

title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
finding: Noncooperative CMARL SR0.75 vs cooperative middle-fusion0.90. Occlusion example and OOD degradation documented. Homogeneous2D LiDAR and short-horizon forecasting are stated limitations.
boundary: Different Unity/LiDAR/cooperation protocol from no-communication Social-HM3D. Cannot rank against NavThinker numbers.
